elements.element: Customer has no obligation to disclose to Vendor any more favourable third-party commercial offer.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 expressly states that Customer “is not required to disclose” any more favourable commercial offer it receives.

elements.element: Customer has no obligation to match for Vendor any more favourable third-party commercial offer.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 expressly states that Customer “is not required to…match for Vendor” any more favourable commercial offer it receives.

elements.element: If an MFN obligation burdens Customer, it is limited to a specifically defined product.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: Section 7.2 imposes no MFN obligation and instead expressly disclaims the disclosure and matching duties.

elements.element: If an MFN obligation burdens Customer, it lasts no more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Section 7.2 imposes no MFN obligation. Accordingly, there is no MFN duration exceeding 12 months.

elements.element: If an MFN obligation burdens Customer, it applies only to reasonably comparable offers and excludes offers that are not reasonably comparable.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Section 7.2 imposes no MFN obligation. No non-comparable offer is subject to disclosure or matching.

result.reason: The redline fully reaches the preferred position by expressly negating both operative burdens in the original clause: disclosure and matching. The fallback is also satisfied because its limitations are conditional on an MFN obligation existing, and the rendered clause demonstrably imposes none. The change is confined to Section 7.2, leaves Section 7.1 intact, and introduces no unrelated obligation or contradiction. Drafting is effective, though retaining the introductory phrase “Before engaging another provider” is slightly awkward and deletion of Section 7.2 would have been cleaner.
